$comment: Root ADR-0175. The Cloudflare Workers the data host deploys by itself, and nothing else: scripts/deploy/worker-autodeploy.py deploys exactly the entries here and refuses an entry whose Wrangler config names another Worker. The Cloudflare account holds other scripts; they are not listed, so they are never touched. Names, hostnames, paths and the preview Worker are read from the entry's gateway block in config/r2-connections.contract.json (gateway, preview), never restated here; inputs are the paths whose bytes make up the Worker, so a change to any of them deploys it again. A smoke is what a deploy must see from the Worker's hostname before it counts: by-pnu reads the gateway's capabilities path until the answer names the new version, then runs the edge probe (scripts/ops/by-pnu-edge-probe.py, root ADR-0327: every lane the Worker serves and its media, GET twice) and the lane's serving monitor against that hostname; http asks for one path and expects one status. containers holds the cap of the one container a deploy runs (tools/host-memory-budget.contract.json one_shot_contracts).

smoke.reason: a pack-only lane (root ADR-0190) is held to its serving monitor once it is cut over, like the parcel and building lanes. Before its first publish every PNU is a 503 and the monitor has nothing to read, so while the lane's monitor file (runtime-secrets group unit-price-serving-monitor, written by the operator's monitor-sample step of the cut-over) does not exist its smoke is the capabilities read alone

a source id of the contract's shape whose archive does not exist: the Worker parses the path and asks the bucket, so a 404 needs the new code and its R2 binding to answer; a release id changes with every bake, so no 200 path stays true

the gateway block names no hostname (the custom domain is attached in the dashboard and the Wrangler config has no routes, so a deploy leaves it alone); an artifact id of the contract's shape that no profile has, which the Worker looks up in the bucket
the public overlay read answers 200 from D1 whether or not edits are pending

monitor_latency.reason: a by-PNU smoke's monitor holds a p95 bound that the live hostname can breach with no help from the new version: on 2026-10-12 the zone's Korean traffic moved to another edge and the unchanged production hostnames read at p95 3.7-9.9 s against a 3 s bound, so three Workers gave up. When only the p95 breaches (every PNU answered with the document the lane serves), the deployer reads the same sample from the other hostname of the Worker (the preview is compared with production, which still serves the version before; production with the preview, which already passed) and then again from this one, both warm (root ADR-0154: R2 temperature dominates a cold read), and blocks only when this one is slower than this ratio of the other's p95 and above the bound

attempts_reason: a Worker whose deploy failed is tried again on the next ticks while it is still behind (an npm or Cloudflare API blip should not wait for the next merge), at most this many times for the same inputs; then it waits for a change to its inputs, quietly. Each failed attempt alerts once through the unit's OnFailure

wrangler.memory_reason: pnpm install of one gateway and an esbuild bundle by Wrangler; not measured on the host yet. A Worker deploy is one container at a time
